$what: Provenance of aurora-effects-scene.schema.json — empyrean's CONTRACT schema, vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. scene.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/effects-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_only_a_test_const: Until 2026-08-29 the pinned blob hash lived as a `const PINNED_BLOB` in effects-schema-drift.test.ts and as prose in scene.ts's header and in effects-scene-golden.test.ts's header. Three copies, one of which (scene.ts) had already gone THREE re-pins stale without anything going red, because nothing hashes a comment. The hash now lives HERE, once, and the test reads it. The prose citations remain prose and say so.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path-probe design would degrade to 'schema not found -> skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate and the currency check below are the payment. See docs/reviews/2026-08-28-golden-live-tree.md for the defect that made reading a peer's LIVE WORKING TREE unacceptable — this file is never read from ../empyrean at runtime or at test time by path, only through git objects at a named revision.
$why_not_under_test_fixtures: This is a SOURCE file the app imports, not a test fixture, so it lives beside its consumer. It is also deliberately outside test/fixtures/ because the published-revision sweep in test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts walks that tree and reads every 40-hex on a `revision*` key as an AEON revision; an empyrean SHA sitting there would be checked for reachability from aeon's master and fail for a reason that has nothing to do with it.

Reading 1, parsed leaf diff: 19 ADDED, 0 removed, 0 changed-in-place, 263 leaves before and 282 after, and EVERY added pointer is under /$defs/layer/properties/rowRemap. what_changed_at_this_pin.nineteen_not_seventeen_and_why_the_diffe: ⚠ A LEAF DIFF THAT FLATTENS TO SCALARS CANNOT SEE `"not": {}`. The CR was relayed to this lane as SEVENTEEN leaf additions; the instrument here reports NINETEEN. The two extra are /$defs/layer/properties/rowRemap/oneOf/1/properties/ladder/not and .../table/not, whose value is an EMPTY OBJECT — a container with no scalar under it, so a pointer-to-scalar walk emits nothing for it and the node is invisible. That is not a bookkeeping quibble: those two invisible nodes ARE the refusal mechanism this amendment adds, so an instrument blind to them would report the reserved-name rulings as absent. `schema-revendor-proof.mjs` prints such a node as `<empty object>` and therefore sees them; its own header names this exact blindness as the reason it takes TWO readings. Counted here rather than relayed.
what_changed_at_this_pin.the_hazard_this_pin_carries: TWO UNITS AND A THIRD COORDINATE SPACE, ON ONE TWO-FIELD PAYLOAD. (1) `height_shift` IS A SHIFT, NOT A LINE COUNT — H = 1 << shift, so an editor presenting "64 lines" must EXPORT 6. The contract states the rule in its own words ("an editor may DISPLAY 1 << height_shift beside the control and MUST EXPORT the shift") and aeon's ensure names the trap ("If you meant 64 LINES, you want 6"). EVERY value 3..7 IS LEGAL, so a conversion bug lands as a band four times too tall, never as a refusal — no build can catch it. Aurora shows the line count and writes the shift, and the << lives exactly once, in `rowRemapHeightLines`. (2) `plane_y` IS A PLANE-B LINE (the `vsplit.at` space), not a world Y and not a screen line — a THIRD coordinate space on a surface that already reconciles two. (3) THIS SCHEMA IS THE ONLY ENFORCEMENT OF THE 511 CEILING ANYWHERE: aeon's ensure at scene_dsl.emp:1008 tests >= 0 only and brm_plane_y is u16, so 512..65535 emits a silently-wrong window (aeon's own booked row ROWREMAP-PLANEY-CEILING). The usual "the engine already refuses it" argument is INVERTED for this field, and Aurora's control must not lean on a build that will not catch it. (4) SCHEMA-LEGAL IS NOT BUILDABLE: only `height_shift: 4` has a ladder today (row_remap_ladder16(), aeon parallax_dsl.emp:220), so four of the five legal shifts fail aeon's build by name until 9b's generator lands.
what_changed_at_this_pin.aurora_edits_this_pin_forced: (1) NOTHING IN json-schema-subset.ts, AND THAT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED: the keyword-coverage gate, the whole-schema walk (assertSchemaSupported) and the per-node check all stayed GREEN against the newly vendored bytes. `const`, `oneOf` and `not` were already implemented, and `not: {}` needed nothing new because the evaluator's `not` validates its subschema and inverts — an empty subschema matches everything, so the inversion refuses everything, which is the idiom's meaning. Exercised on a real document rather than argued: a layer carrying `ladder` or `table` inside `rowRemap` is REFUSED by the vendored schema (test/formats/effects-row-remap.test.ts). (2) THE SHAPE-COVERAGE GOLDEN test/fixtures/effects/canopy_dusk.json HAD TO GAIN THE KEY, because effects-scene-golden.test.ts derives 'every declared LAYER key is exercised' from the schema and went red naming `rowRemap` — the gate working as designed. It carries aeon's own shipped values, {plane_y 101, height_shift 4} (games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_scenes.emp:252 at aeon d8baf84f), so the fixture is the corpus rather than a pair of numbers this repo invented. (3) EffectsLayer gained `rowRemap?: EffectsRowRemap` in scene.ts; the codec needed no other change, because parse and serialize are schema-driven and `EFFECTS_LAYER_KEY_DEFAULTS` reads the `"none"` default straight out of the new node.
